models.note: TransientModel (wizard). Fields: res_model (Char), file (Binary, raw not base64), file_name (Char), file_type (Char). ~31 methods: the whole parse/map/coerce/load engine. _transient_max_hours=12.0.
Persistent model. Fields: res_model (Char, indexed), column_name (Char), field_name (Char). Remembers external-column -> Odoo-field choices per model so repeat imports from the same source auto-map.

models._description: AbstractModel _inherit='base' adds get_import_templates() hook returning [{label, template}] used to surface per-model sample templates in the wizard.
Adds _can_import_remote_urls() gate (admin-only by default) controlling whether a user may pull binary/image fields from remote URLs (DOS guard).

views.note: No Python/XML business views: the entire wizard UI is an OWL client action (tag 'import'), see frontend.

behavioral_notes.observation: The file-sniffing + mapping-suggestion entrypoint. _read_file dispatches by guessed mimetype (guess_mimetype) then by user-provided type then by file extension to format readers. _read_csv uses chardet.detect to auto-guess encoding (rectifying BOM-marked utf-16/32), then auto-detects the delimiter by trying ',',';','tab',' ','|' and unit-separator and keeping the candidate that yields uniform-width rows >=2 cols. XLS/XLSX/ODS go through xlrd/openpyxl/odf readers that coerce numbers/dates per cell type. parse_preview then builds the importable-fields tree (get_fields_tree, recursive to depth 3 over relations), extracts per-column candidate types from the 10-row preview (_extract_header_types heuristics: __export__ -> id/relational, digits -> int/float/monetary/bool, true/false -> bool, float patterns, date/datetime pattern matching), and proposes a column->field mapping. None of this dialect/encoding sniffing is visible in metadata.

Three-tier column-to-field matching: (1) look up a previously saved base_import.mapping for this res_model (distance forced to -1 so it always wins); (2) exact case-folded match on field technical name, on the model's @string label, and on the en_US label; (3) fuzzy match using word distance (1 - difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio) against fields pre-filtered by the column's inferred types, accepting the closest below FUZZY_MATCH_DISTANCE=0.2. Deduplication then guarantees at most one column per simple field (smallest distance wins), while '/'-joined relational paths (e.g. partner_id/name) are matched recursively and exempt from dedup. This fuzzy/translation-aware matching is pure runtime behaviour.

_convert_import_data drops unmapped columns (itemgetter on the kept indices), validates that every row width equals the header width (else a 'change the separator' UserError), strips the header row, removes empty rows, and applies the 'skip' offset. _parse_import_data recurses the field tree and coerces in place: dates/datetimes via strptime against the chosen/guessed format; floats via _parse_float_from_data which strips currency symbols (_remove_currency_symbol checks res.currency symbols), infers thousand/decimal separators, and handles ()-negatives and scientific notation; binary/attachment columns are validated as URL vs base64 vs filename. Coercion failures raise ImportValidationError carrying field + field_type so the client can attach the error to the right column. This data-cleaning layer is the core value metadata cannot show.

behavioral_notes.element: execute_import -> model.load() (transactional load, dryrun, relational name-resolution)
behavioral_notes.observation:
Wraps the load in a savepoint. Calls _convert_import_data + _parse_import_data, _extract_binary_filenames, _handle_multi_mapping (concatenates multiple columns mapped to one char/text/html field by space/newline/
, many2many by comma), and _handle_fallback_values (substitutes a chosen default when a selection/boolean value is out of range). It then calls self.env[res_model].load(import_fields, data) with context import_file=True, name_create_enabled_fields (lets unknown many2one/many2many values be name_create'd on the fly), import_set_empty_fields, import_skip_records and _import_limit (batching). The ORM load() does the relational name-search resolution (matching 'Acme' to a res.partner id, or External/Database IDs). dryrun=True rolls the savepoint back and clears caches so a 'Test' run surfaces every row error without writing. On success it persists base_import.mapping rows for reuse. Returns {ids, messages:[{type,message,record,rows,field_path}], nextrow, name, binary_filenames} which the OWL client renders per-column / per-row.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend: ImportAction OWL client action (static/src) -- THE wizard UI (gap #3)
behavioral_notes.observation: The entire Import Records experience is OWL/JS, not Python views (10 JS / 8 XML files). registry.category('actions').add('import', ImportAction) registers a client action; ImportRecords adds an 'Import records' item to the cogMenu of every list/kanban view (gated on the view's import= and create= attributes). ImportAction hosts FileInput + dropzone upload (csv/xls/xlsx), ImportDataContent (per-column field pickers populated from get_fields_tree, sorted into Basic/Suggested/Additional/Relational), ImportDataSidepanel (CSV options: encoding, separator, quoting, date/datetime/thousands/decimal formats, skip, limit, sheet), ImportDataProgress (batched progress + pause/resume), ImportDataColumnError, ImportBlockUI. BaseImportModel (import_model.js) drives the round-trips: POST /base_import/set_file to upload, orm.call base_import.import.parse_preview for the preview+mapping, then chunked orm.call execute_import with dryrun for 'Test' then real import, translating human date formats to Python strftime and back. This is the canonical metadata-gap-#3 subsystem: zero business views, all behaviour in static assets.

integrations.note: The only outbound HTTP is _import_file_by_url: when a binary/image column holds a URL, requests.Session().get() fetches it (admin-gated via res.users._can_import_remote_urls, size/timeout/pixel-capped via import_file_maxbytes / import_file_timeout / import_url_regex config). No third-party SDK or API key.

runtime.note: base_import.import is a transient (wizard) model (rows are ephemeral, GC'd after 12h); base_import.mapping rows accrue only as users perform imports. Not run live in this pass.

it_architecture.application: base_import (CSV/XLS/XLSX/ODS data-import framework: file-sniffing parser, fuzzy column->field matcher, type-coercion engine, transactional loader, and the OWL 'Import Records' wizard reused by every list/kanban view)
software_services: /base_import/set_file (HTTP POST: upload raw file bytes onto the base_import.import wizard record)
base_import.import.parse_preview (RPC: sniff dialect/encoding, build field tree, suggest mapping, return preview)
base_import.import.execute_import (RPC: coerce + load via model.load(), dryrun test or real import, return per-row/per-column errors)
base_import.import.get_fields_tree (RPC: recursive importable-field tree for a model)
base.get_import_templates (RPC hook: per-model sample import templates)
logical_data_erm: base_import.import.res_model -> (any ir.model, by name) target model being imported into
base_import.mapping (res_model, column_name) -> field_name : remembered column->field mapping per model
execute_import -> <res_model>.load() : writes records into ANY target model (no FK; dynamic by res_model)
information_flows: depends: web (OWL client action, registries, orm service, FileInput/dropzone)
upload: browser -> POST /base_import/set_file -> write file bytes onto base_import.import
preview: OWL BaseImportModel -> parse_preview -> chardet/csv/xlrd/openpyxl/odf readers + get_fields_tree + fuzzy matcher -> preview+mapping back to client
load: OWL -> execute_import -> _convert/_parse/_handle_multi_mapping/_handle_fallback -> env[res_model].load() -> ORM create/write + relational name resolution
outbound (optional): _parse_import_data -> requests.get(url) for remote binary/image columns (admin-gated)
feedback: load() returns {ids, messages, nextrow, name, binary_filenames} -> OWL renders per-column ImportDataColumnError + per-row messages; successful mapping persisted to base_import.mapping
frontend_components: ImportAction (OWL client action, registry tag 'import', mounts the wizard)
ImportRecords (cogMenu 'Import records' entry on every list/kanban view)

capabilities: Ingest tabular data files (CSV / XLS / XLSX / ODS) with auto encoding & delimiter detection
Auto-suggest & remember column-to-field mappings (exact + translation + fuzzy matching)
Coerce & validate import values (dates, floats/currency, booleans, selection, binary/URL/base64)
Resolve relational references on load (External ID, Database ID, name-search, on-the-fly name_create)
Dry-run ('Test') import with full error reporting before committing
Batched / resumable bulk load with per-column and per-row error feedback
Provide the reusable 'Import Records' UI surfaced on every list/kanban view
value_streams: File-to-Records: upload file -> sniff & preview -> map columns -> Test (dryrun) -> resolve errors -> commit load -> open imported records
Map-Reuse: successful import -> persist base_import.mapping -> next import from same source auto-maps columns
information_concepts: field tree (importable fields of the target model)
import options (encoding/separator/quoting/date/float formats, skip, limit, sheet)
policies: res.users._can_import_remote_urls(): URL-based binary/image import restricted to admin by default (worker-DOS guard)
Remote-fetch caps: import_file_maxbytes / import_file_timeout / import_url_regex config; 42 MP image ceiling
Test-before-commit: dryrun rolls back the savepoint and clears caches so no partial writes leak
readonly/magic-column fields excluded from the importable field tree
stakeholders: Data-migration / onboarding consultant (loads legacy master data into a new database)
Functional / power user (bulk-updates records from a spreadsheet)
System administrator (governs remote-URL imports and file-size limits)
Module developer (exposes get_import_templates / import= view attribute)
metrics: Rows imported per run (import_result ids count) and nextrow resume offset
Mapping match quality (fuzzy distance vs FUZZY_MATCH_DISTANCE threshold)
Error counts surfaced per column/row in the test run

classification.rationale: base_import is a cross-cutting data-management framework, not a value-creating primary activity of any chain/shop/network. It owns no business object of its own (its only persistent model, base_import.mapping, is mapping metadata; base_import.import is a transient wizard) and instead acts ON every other model via a dynamic res_model + env[model].load(). It is firm IT infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'): auto_install=true and depends only on web, and the cogMenu 'Import Records' entry is injected into every list/kanban view. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits because the work is data management / master-data loading -- the IT-delivery capability of ingesting, cleansing, mapping and loading data into the application platform. 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was considered (it underpins onboarding of every other capability) but rejected: base_import is a concrete running data-loading utility, not a governance/portfolio capability; its substance is IT data-management, squarely 8.0. Mirrors the 'web' classification (support / 8.0): both are data-bearing-inverse framework modules whose substance is plumbing reused by all apps.

standard_capabilities: Import CSV / XLS / XLSX / ODS into ANY importable model out of the box
Automatic encoding (chardet) and CSV delimiter detection
Exact + translation-aware + fuzzy column-to-field mapping with saved-mapping reuse
Type coercion: dates/datetimes (format guessing), floats with currency symbol & separator inference, booleans, selection fallbacks
Relational resolution by External ID, Database ID, name-search, and on-the-fly name_create
Test (dryrun) import with full per-column / per-row error reporting before committing
Batched, resumable bulk import with progress + pause/resume
typical_fits: Initial data migration / onboarding: load partners, products, contacts, BoMs, etc. from spreadsheets
Recurring loads from a third-party system (saved mappings auto-apply)
Bulk record updates by importing with id / External ID columns
common_gaps: Complex transformations / cleansing beyond format coercion (needs ETL or pre-processing)
Cross-record deduplication / upsert logic beyond id-based matching
Custom OWL wizard steps or bespoke validation (requires JS dev, gap #3)
Scheduled / unattended imports (the wizard is interactive; no built-in cron import here)
Very large files: batching helps but worker memory / timeout limits still apply
